class AR(y: VectorD, hh: Int, tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ..., adjusted: Boolean = ..., tForm: Transform = ...) extends Forecaster, Correlogram, NoSubModels

The AR class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for Auto-Regressive (AR) models. AR models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = combination of last p values.

The AR class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for Auto-Regressive (AR) models. AR models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = combination of last p values.

y_t = δ +  b ∙ [ y_t-p, ... y_t-2, y_t-1 ] + e_t
y_t = δ + b_0 y_t-p + ... + b_p-2 y_t-2 + b_p-1 y_t-1 + e_t

where y_t is the value of y at time t and e_t is the residual/error term.

Value parameters

adjusted

whether in Correlogram when calculating auto-covariances/auto-correlations to adjust to account for the number of elements in the sum Σ (or use dim-1)

bakcast

whether a backcasted value is prepended to the time series (defaults to false)

hh

the maximum forecasting horizon (h = 1 to hh)

hparam

the hyper-parameters (defaults to AR.hp)

tRng

the time range, if relevant (time index may suffice)

y

the response vector (time series data)

class ARMA(y: VectorD, hh: Int, tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ...) extends Forecaster

The ARMA class fits an Auto-Regressive Moving Average model using a state-space representation and Kalman-filter maximum likelihood.

The ARMA class fits an Auto-Regressive Moving Average model using a state-space representation and Kalman-filter maximum likelihood.

Model: y_t = c + Σ_j φ_j y_{t-j} + Σ_k θ_k e_{t-k} + e_t

The implementation estimates:

  • AR coefficients φ
  • MA coefficients θ
  • intercept c
  • process variance σ² Notes:
  • The likelihood is computed from one-step-ahead Kalman innovations.
  • A small burn-in (max(p, q+1)) is excluded from the log-likelihood sum to align with the external reference implementation.
  • Rolling forecast evaluation is performed externally in the test driver.

Value parameters

bakcast

whether a backcast value is prepended

hh

the maximum forecast horizon

hparam

the hyper-parameters

tRng

the optional time range

y

the response/time-series vector

The ARMA_2SL class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for Auto-Regressive, Moving Average (ARMA_2SL) models. ARMA_2SL models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = combination of last p values and q shocks.

class ARMA_KF(y: VectorD, hh: Int, tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ...) extends Forecaster, NoSubModels

The ARMA_KF class fits an ARMA(p, q) model via Kalman-filter maximum- likelihood estimation (KF-MLE) using the PACF stationarity reparameterization.

The ARMA_KF class fits an ARMA(p, q) model via Kalman-filter maximum- likelihood estimation (KF-MLE) using the PACF stationarity reparameterization.

Unconstrained parameter vector optimised by L-BFGS-B: u = [ u₁..u_p, v₁..v_q, μ, ℓ ] where: φ_i = DL(tanh(u_i)) — AR coefficients via Durbin-Levinson (stationary) θ_i = DL(tanh(v_i)) — MA coefficients via Durbin-Levinson (invertible) μ = process mean (optimised directly) σ² = exp(ℓ) — process variance (always positive)

After training, the model exposes the full Forecaster interface:

  • predict(t, y_): sequential 1-step-ahead KF prediction
  • forecast(t, y_): multi-step projection from the running KF state
  • forecastAt(h, y_): full fresh-pass h-step forecast for all time points

Value parameters

bakcast

whether to prepend a backcast value (default false)

hh

the maximum forecast horizon

hparam

the hyper-parameters (p, q)

tRng

the optional time range

y

the response/time-series vector

The ARMA_Stability object allows stability of ARMA (p, q) coefficient φ and θ values to be checked to make sure the roots of the characteristic polynomial are outside the unit circle. It they are not, the fitted model may be unstable with poor accuracy in certain cases.

class ARP(y: VectorD, hh: Int, tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ..., adjusted: Boolean = ..., tForm: Transform = ..., resample: Boolean = ...) extends AR

The ARP class extends AR to provide probabilistic forecasting with prediction intervals. It computes MA(∞) impulse response coefficients (ψ weights) from the fitted AR(p) parameters φ, then uses them to derive the theoretically correct h-step-ahead forecast error variance:

The ARP class extends AR to provide probabilistic forecasting with prediction intervals. It computes MA(∞) impulse response coefficients (ψ weights) from the fitted AR(p) parameters φ, then uses them to derive the theoretically correct h-step-ahead forecast error variance:

σ²_h = σ²_e * Σ (ψ²_j,  j = 0, 1, ..., h-1)

where ψ_0 = 1 and ψ_j = Σ_i φ_i * ψ_{j-i} for j >= 1.

Value parameters

adjusted

whether in Correlogram when calculating auto-covariances/auto-correlations to adjust to account for the number of elements in the sum Σ (or use dim-1)

bakcast

whether a backcasted value is prepended to the time series (defaults to false)

hh

the maximum forecasting horizon (h = 1 to hh)

hparam

the hyper-parameters (defaults to AR.hp)

resample

whether to use the empirical re-sampling or theoretical method

tForm

the transformation applied

tRng

the time range, if relevant (time index may suffice)

y

the response vector (time series data)

class ARX_SR(x: MatrixD, y: VectorD, hh: Int, n_exo: Int, fname: Array[String], tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ..., tForms: TransformMap = ..., fExo_sz: Array[Int] = ...) extends ARX

The ARX_SR class provides time series analysis capabilities for ARX Symbolic Regression (SR) models. These models include trend, linear, power, root, and cross terms for the single endogenous (y) variable and zero or more exogenous (xe) variables. Given time series data stored in vector y and matrix xe, its next value y_t = combination of last p values of y, y^p, y^r and the last q values of each exogenous variable xe_j, again in linear, power and root forms (as well as ENDO-EXO cross terms).

The ARX_SR class provides time series analysis capabilities for ARX Symbolic Regression (SR) models. These models include trend, linear, power, root, and cross terms for the single endogenous (y) variable and zero or more exogenous (xe) variables. Given time series data stored in vector y and matrix xe, its next value y_t = combination of last p values of y, y^p, y^r and the last q values of each exogenous variable xe_j, again in linear, power and root forms (as well as ENDO-EXO cross terms).

y_t = b dot x_t + e_t

where y_t is the value of y at time t, x_t is a vector of inputs, and e_t is the residual/error term.

Value parameters

bakcast

whether a backcasted value is prepended to the time series (defaults to false)

fExo_sz

the array of the number of transformations for each exogenous

fname

the feature/variable names

hh

the maximum forecasting horizon (h = 1 to hh)

hparam

the hyper-parameters (defaults to AR.hp)

n_exo

the number of exogenous variables

tForms

the map of transformations applied

tRng

the time range, if relevant (time index may suffice)

x

the data/input matrix (lagged columns of y and xe) @see ARX_SR.apply

y

the response/output vector (main time series data)

The ARY class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for ARY models. ARY models utilize multiple linear regression based on lagged values of y and optional trend terms (@see spec). Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = combination of last p values of y.

The ARY class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for ARY models. ARY models utilize multiple linear regression based on lagged values of y and optional trend terms (@see spec). Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = combination of last p values of y.

y_t = b ∙ x_t + e_t
x_t = [ y_t-p, ... y_t-2, y_t-1 ]  when spec = 0

where y_t is the value of y at time t and e_t is the residual/error term. x_t consists of optional trend terms and past/lagged y-values (@see ARY.buildMatrix)

the map of transformations applied

trait Filter(y: VectorD)

The Filter trait provides basic time series capabilities for filters. A filter is used to pull out the important information from a time series. Commonly, this involves improving the signal-to-noise ratio, which is often accomplished by using a low-pass filter that remove high frequencies. Such filters are also called smoothers (the smoothed time series has less abrupt changes)

class KalmanFilterKF(val f: MatrixD, val q: MatrixD, val h: MatrixD, val r: MatrixD, var x: VectorD, var p: MatrixD)

The KalmanFilterKF class is a minimal Kalman filter used by ARMA_KF for Kalman-Filter maximum-likelihood estimation (KF-MLE).

The KalmanFilterKF class is a minimal Kalman filter used by ARMA_KF for Kalman-Filter maximum-likelihood estimation (KF-MLE).

It differs from the general KalmanFilter in this package in one essential way: predict() advances the public state x and covariance p IN PLACE, so the predicted (prior) state is readable on x/p between predict() and update(). ARMA_KF reads x/p at exactly that point to accumulate the Gaussian log-likelihood, so it requires this in-place semantics. (The general KalmanFilter instead stashes the prediction in private xPred/pPred and leaves x/p at the previous posterior — correct for its simulation use, but unusable for KF-MLE.) Kept as a separate class so ARMA.scala and the KalmanFilter simulation tests are unaffected.

Value parameters

f

the state transition matrix

h

the measurement matrix

p

the initial covariance matrix (advanced in place by predict/update)

q

the process noise covariance matrix

r

the measurement noise covariance matrix

x

the initial state vector (advanced in place by predict/update)

The NullModel class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for NullModel models. NullModel models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = mean may be predicted based on its past value of y:

The NullModel class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for NullModel models. NullModel models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = mean may be predicted based on its past value of y:

y_t = mean + e_t

where mean is the mean of y and e_t is the new residual/error term.

Value parameters

bakcast

the maximum forecasting horizon (h = 1 to hh)

the hyper-parameters (none => use null)

the time range, if relevant (time index may suffice)

y

the response vector (time series data)

The RandomWalk class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for RandomWalk models. RandomWalk models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t+1 = y(t+1) may be predicted based on its past value of y:

The RandomWalk class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for RandomWalk models. RandomWalk models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t+1 = y(t+1) may be predicted based on its past value of y:

y_t+1 = y_t + e_t+1

The RandomWalkS class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for RandomWalkS models. RandomWalkS models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t is the previous value adjusted by the slope weighted by s.

The RandomWalkS class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for RandomWalkS models. RandomWalkS models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t is the previous value adjusted by the slope weighted by s.

y_t = y_t-1 + s (y_t-1 - y_t-2) + e_t

where y_t is the value of y at time t and e_t is the residual/error term.

class SARY(x: MatrixD, y: VectorD, hh: Int, fname: Array[String], tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ...) extends ARY

The SARY class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for SARY models. These models extend ARY models by including seasonal (periodic) lags. SARY models utilize multiple linear regression based on lagged values of y. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = combination of the last p lagged values of y and the last ps seasonally lagged values.

The SARY class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for SARY models. These models extend ARY models by including seasonal (periodic) lags. SARY models utilize multiple linear regression based on lagged values of y. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = combination of the last p lagged values of y and the last ps seasonally lagged values.

y_t = b dot x_t + e_t

where y_t is the value of y at time t, b is the parameter vector, x_t collects past lagged (both regular and seasonal) values, and e_t is the residual/error term.

Value parameters

bakcast

whether a backcasted value is prepended to the time series (defaults to false)

fname

the feature/variable names

hh

the maximum forecasting horizon (h = 1 to hh)

hparam

the hyper-parameters (defaults to AR.hp)

tRng

the time range, if relevant (time index may suffice)

x

the data/input matrix (lagged columns of y) @see SARY.apply

y

the response/output vector (time series data)

The SimpleExpSmoothing class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for Simple Exponential Smoothing models. SimpleExpSmoothing models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = mean of last q values.

class TrendModel(y: VectorD, hh: Int, tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ...) extends Forecaster, NoSubModels

The TrendModel class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for TrendModel models. TrendModel models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = f(t) = b_0 + b_1 t.

The TrendModel class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for TrendModel models. TrendModel models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = f(t) = b_0 + b_1 t.

y_t = f(t) + e_t

where y_t is the value of y at time t and e_t is the residual/error term.

Value parameters

bakcast

whether a backcasted value is prepended to the time series (defaults to false)

hh

the maximum forecasting horizon (h = 1 to hh)

hparam

the hyper-parameters (none => use null)

tRng

the time range, if relevant (time index may suffice)

y

the response vector (time series data)

case class WaveTerm(w: Double, phase: Double, idx: Int = ...) extends Term

The WaveTerm case class represents a seasonal term that is a function of the time index t (not of a data column): sin (w t + phase). Use wave to build the sin/cos pair for a frequency, so the fitted coefficients capture any phase.

The WaveTerm case class represents a seasonal term that is a function of the time index t (not of a data column): sin (w t + phase). Use wave to build the sin/cos pair for a frequency, so the fitted coefficients capture any phase.

Value parameters

idx

the 1-based rank of the frequency in the periodogram list it came from (0 => not from a list), so a formula can write wave(k)

phase

the phase: 0 for the sine component, Pi/2 for the cosine component

w

the angular frequency (2 Pi times the frequency in cycles per time unit)

class WeightedMovingAverage(y: VectorD, hh: Int, tRng: Range = ..., hparam: HyperParameter = ..., bakcast: Boolean = ...) extends SimpleMovingAverage

The WeightedMovingAverage class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for WeightedMovingAverage models. WeightedMovingAverage models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = weighted mean of last q values.

The WeightedMovingAverage class provides basic time series analysis capabilities for WeightedMovingAverage models. WeightedMovingAverage models are often used for forecasting. Given time series data stored in vector y, its next value y_t = weighted mean of last q values.

y_t = weighted-mean (y_t-1, ..., y_t-q) + e_t

where y_t is the value of y at time t and e_t is the residual/error term.

Value parameters

bakcast

whether a backcasted value is prepended to the time series (defaults to false)

hh

the maximum forecasting horizon (h = 1 to hh)

hparam

the hyper-parameters (defaults to SimpleMovingAverage.hp)

tRng

the time range, if relevant (time index may suffice)

y

the response vector (time series data)

Attributes

Companion

def aRIMA_diffTest(): Unit

The aRIMA_diffTest main function tests the ARIMA_diff object on real data: Forecasting lake levels comparing ARMA, AR1MA, Differenced ARMA, Transformed-Back Differenced ARMA. Observe that backform is better than undiff on predictions.

def aRMA_KalmanRollingValidation(): Unit

Rolling-origin validation driver for the standalone Kalman-filter ARMA implementation. The logic mirrors the external Python validation flow:

Rolling-origin validation driver for the standalone Kalman-filter ARMA implementation. The logic mirrors the external Python validation flow:

  • fit once on the training window
  • forecast horizons 1..hh before each newly revealed test observation
  • update the filter state sequentially without refitting

def aRX_DTest10(): Unit

The aRX_DTest10 main function tests the ARX_D class on real data: Forecasting COVID-19 and ILI using Train-n-Test Split (TnT) with Rolling Validation. Test forecasts (h = 1 to hh steps ahead forecasts). This version compares the three ways one column set can be chosen for a multi-horizon model -- selectFeatures (h = 1) (horizon 1 decides), selectFeatures (h = hh) (the last horizon decides) and selectFeatures () (all horizons jointly, J = the mean FPE-form sMAPE) -- keeps the three selected models and runs TnT on all three (and on the full model) at the end, so their QoF blocks can be read side by side.

Test forecasts (h = 1 to hh steps ahead forecasts). runMain scalation.modeling.forecasting.aRX_DTest10

def aRX_DTest11(): Unit

The aRX_DTest11 main function tests ARX_D.fromTerms on real data: Forecasting COVID-19 using Train-n-Test Split (TnT) with Rolling Validation. Test forecasts (h = 1 to hh steps ahead forecasts). The model is built from a FORMULA's terms -- lag windows of y, icu and pRate plus log1p and squared terms -- so skipped lags and transforms that contiguous lags 1 to p cannot express are included; the matrix has no intercept column, hence first = 0. Feature Selection runs over all horizons jointly (J = the mean FPE-form sMAPE) and the selected model is tested with TnT.

The aRX_DTest11 main function tests ARX_D.fromTerms on real data: Forecasting COVID-19 using Train-n-Test Split (TnT) with Rolling Validation. Test forecasts (h = 1 to hh steps ahead forecasts). The model is built from a FORMULA's terms -- lag windows of y, icu and pRate plus log1p and squared terms -- so skipped lags and transforms that contiguous lags 1 to p cannot express are included; the matrix has no intercept column, hence first = 0. Feature Selection runs over all horizons jointly (J = the mean FPE-form sMAPE) and the selected model is tested with TnT.

runMain scalation.modeling.forecasting.aRX_DTest11

def aRX_DTest12(): Unit

The aRX_DTest12 main function tests ARX_D.fromTerms with the training-window contract on the COVID-19 dataset: a model built from a formula on the FULL series is trained on its leading trSize rows only, then its forecast matrix is filled for every row, so the rows from trSize on are out-of-sample. Checks: (1) the fit uses the training rows only: its h = 1 parameters equal those of a CenteredRidgeMV fit directly on the training rows, and that model's original-space intercept and slopes reproduce predict on a testing row, (2) scaled = true with lambda = 0 gives the same forecasts as scaled = false, (3) a standardized response is never rectified and the global hp("nneg") is left alone by fromTerms. Feature selection on a fromTerms matrix is tested by aRX_DTest11.

The aRX_DTest12 main function tests ARX_D.fromTerms with the training-window contract on the COVID-19 dataset: a model built from a formula on the FULL series is trained on its leading trSize rows only, then its forecast matrix is filled for every row, so the rows from trSize on are out-of-sample. Checks: (1) the fit uses the training rows only: its h = 1 parameters equal those of a CenteredRidgeMV fit directly on the training rows, and that model's original-space intercept and slopes reproduce predict on a testing row, (2) scaled = true with lambda = 0 gives the same forecasts as scaled = false, (3) a standardized response is never rectified and the global hp("nneg") is left alone by fromTerms. Feature selection on a fromTerms matrix is tested by aRX_DTest11.

runMain scalation.modeling.forecasting.aRX_DTest12

def aRX_DTest5(): Unit

The aRX_DTest5 main function tests the ARX_D class on real data: Forecasting COVID-19 using In-Sample Testing (In-ST). Test forecasts (h = 1 to hh steps ahead forecasts). This version performs Feature Selection AT HORIZON 1 (selectFeaturesAtH) on a RESCALED model (tFormT = Log1p) and tests the selected single-horizon model in-sample. The single-horizon model at h = 1 is printed first as the reference for reading the selection traces in ORIGINAL space: a Forward trace's last row (the full model) equals that model's in-sample QoF, and its first row (intercept only) is a genuine original-space sMAPE.

The aRX_DTest5 main function tests the ARX_D class on real data: Forecasting COVID-19 using In-Sample Testing (In-ST). Test forecasts (h = 1 to hh steps ahead forecasts). The single-horizon model at h = 1 is printed first as the reference for reading the selection traces in ORIGINAL space: a Forward trace's last row (the full model) equals that model's in-sample QoF, and its first row (intercept only) is a genuine original-space sMAPE.

The aRX_DTest7 main function tests the ARX_D class on real data: Forecasting COVID-19 using In-Sample Testing (In-ST). Test forecasts (h = 1 to hh steps ahead forecasts). This version performs Feature Selection over ALL HORIZONS JOINTLY (selectFeatures, h = 0): every candidate column set is fit as ONE multi-horizon model and scored by J, the mean FPE-form sMAPE over the horizons (Forecaster_D.aggFPE, also the selection score of structure searches). def aRX_DTest9(): Unit

def datasetsTest(): Unit

The datasetsTest main function builds the file-based Covid-19 configuration: the pool comes from the file's header through ExoScreen.pool (the five running totals dropped, excess mortality and new cases excluded), and the configuration's shortlist (ExoMode.Auto, k = 2, maxLag = 6: the defaults of a formula search) must be what exoScreenTest2 finds: hospital patients and the positivity rate. The baseline formula string and the blind names are built on that pool.

The datasetsTest main function builds the file-based Covid-19 configuration: the pool comes from the file's header through ExoScreen.pool (the five running totals dropped, excess mortality and new cases excluded), and the configuration's shortlist (ExoMode.Auto, k = 2, maxLag = 6: the defaults of a formula search) must be what exoScreenTest2 finds: hospital patients and the positivity rate. The baseline formula string and the blind names are built on that pool.

runMain scalation.modeling.forecasting.datasetsTest

def eDA4TSTest(): Unit

The eDA4TSTest main function tests the EDA4TS class on a synthetic series with a planted structure: y depends on its own lag 1, on z at lag 2 (positive) and has a 12-step cycle, so the profile must find the PACF spike at lag 1, the best lag 2 with a positive sign for z, and a period near 12; a wrong model (ARX_D with p = 1 and no exogenous variable, i.e., y ~= y~1) must fail at least one residual test. (rev4.1: the prompt-block check moved to lLMProposerTest.)

The eDA4TSTest main function tests the EDA4TS class on a synthetic series with a planted structure: y depends on its own lag 1, on z at lag 2 (positive) and has a 12-step cycle, so the profile must find the PACF spike at lag 1, the best lag 2 with a positive sign for z, and a period near 12; a wrong model (ARX_D with p = 1 and no exogenous variable, i.e., y ~= y~1) must fail at least one residual test. (rev4.1: the prompt-block check moved to lLMProposerTest.)

def exoScreenTest(): Unit

The exoScreenTest main function screens a pool of nine Covid-19 columns for the weekly deaths on the training rows (Model.trSize of 116 = 92). What the data alone says: excess mortality (ccf 0.863 at lag 1) and new cases (0.814 at lag 2) come first, hospital and icu patients (lag 1) and the positivity rate (lag 3) follow; tests per case and new vaccinations correlate negatively. Excess mortality is another count of the same deaths (one week ahead by the reporting delay), which no statistic can tell from a driver, and new cases are not comparable over the period (testing regimes changed), so both are excluded by domain knowledge -- as in Example_Covid, which never uses them. Then the shortlist of two is hospital patients and the positivity rate, i.e., BEST2_EXO with hospital load in place of icu load (collinear, 0.989 > thr2); with three kept, tests per case join (negative). Last, the same Model.screen with its default lag-0 dependency shows why the lead matters: it would take new tests before the positivity rate, which leads deaths by three weeks (2nd by lead, only 4th alongside).

The exoScreenTest main function screens a pool of nine Covid-19 columns for the weekly deaths on the training rows (Model.trSize of 116 = 92). What the data alone says: excess mortality (ccf 0.863 at lag 1) and new cases (0.814 at lag 2) come first, hospital and icu patients (lag 1) and the positivity rate (lag 3) follow; tests per case and new vaccinations correlate negatively. Excess mortality is another count of the same deaths (one week ahead by the reporting delay), which no statistic can tell from a driver, and new cases are not comparable over the period (testing regimes changed), so both are excluded by domain knowledge -- as in Example_Covid, which never uses them. Then the shortlist of two is hospital patients and the positivity rate, i.e., BEST2_EXO with hospital load in place of icu load (collinear, 0.989 > thr2); with three kept, tests per case join (negative). Last, the same Model.screen with its default lag-0 dependency shows why the lead matters: it would take new tests before the positivity rate, which leads deaths by three weeks (2nd by lead, only 4th alongside).

runMain scalation.modeling.forecasting.exoScreenTest

Attributes

def exoScreenTest2(): Unit

The exoScreenTest2 main function does the whole screening automatically from the file: MatrixD.loadH reads covid_19_weekly.csv with its header (the date column skipped), the rows every Covid-19 test uses are kept (0 until 116, @see Example_Covid.clip), pool decides which of the 15 other columns are eligible (the five running totals -- people vaccinated, fully vaccinated, boosters, and the two cumulative excess-mortality columns -- are dropped as cumulative), and shortlist picks from what is left. Nothing about the columns is written in the test except the response's name and, in the second part, the two domain exclusions (excess mortality, new cases); the outcome must equal exoScreenTest's.

The exoScreenTest2 main function does the whole screening automatically from the file: MatrixD.loadH reads covid_19_weekly.csv with its header (the date column skipped), the rows every Covid-19 test uses are kept (0 until 116, @see Example_Covid.clip), pool decides which of the 15 other columns are eligible (the five running totals -- people vaccinated, fully vaccinated, boosters, and the two cumulative excess-mortality columns -- are dropped as cumulative), and shortlist picks from what is left. Nothing about the columns is written in the test except the response's name and, in the second part, the two domain exclusions (excess mortality, new cases); the outcome must equal exoScreenTest's.

runMain scalation.modeling.forecasting.exoScreenTest2

def exoScreenTest3(): Unit

The exoScreenTest3 main function is the user's path from a file to a forecaster in three lines: load the file with its header, screen it for the response and k, build the model on what was chosen (excess mortality and new cases excluded, as everywhere). With k = 3 the chosen columns come back in the file's order (hospital patients, positivity rate, tests per case); the ARX_D model on the k = 2 choice -- hospital patients and the positivity rate, BEST2_EXO with hospital for icu load -- is then trained and tested exactly as in aRX_DTest4 (TnT with rolling validation), so its sMAPE can be set against the BEST2_EXO run.

The formulaParserTest2 main function tests that every grammar production is the ARX_Formula DSL: each specification string, parsed, must build the same ARX_D design matrix (ARX_D.fromTerms) as the DSL formula written by hand -- the parser calls the DSL's own term constructors -- and each DSL formula must serialize (formulaStr) back to a string that parses to the same key, so DSL formulas can seed the search. Uses the Covid-19 BEST2_EXO data (icu patients, test positivity rate).

Uses the Covid-19 BEST2_EXO data (icu patients, test positivity rate).

the max forecasting horizon

whether to use test set or full dataset

mod

the model to be evaluated

qk

index of Quality of Fit (QoF) to use for comparing quality

swap

whether to allow a swap step (swap out a feature for a new feature in one step)

toFile

whether to send to stdout or to a file

The stationaryTest3 main function tests the Stationary class on a simulated stationary time-series. An AR(2) is a stationary process when |φ_2| < 1 and |φ_1| < 1 - φ_2, a unit root process when |φ_2| = 1 or |φ_1| = 1 - φ_2, and explosive otherwise.

def ↑(p: Double): Term

Power operators on terms: ↑ (power) and ↟ (sign-safe power), e.g., y~1 ↑ 0.67. They are Scala sugar for pow and powr (same terms, same labels) and bind tighter than +, so no parentheses are needed in a formula.
